healthcareSystem: Mixed public/private. Public hospitals provide basic care; private hospitals and clinics in Cairo, Alexandria, and resort areas offer excellent quality at reasonable prices.
qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Cairo and Alexandria offer good quality care comparable to Western standards at a fraction of the cost. Public hospitals are basic and under-resourced. Many private doctors speak English and/or French. Pharmacies (pharmacies) are widely available, often open late.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 9am-11pm; many 24-hour pharmacies in major cities; pharmacy chains include Oscar, Seif, and Nile Pharmacies
pharmacyTips: Many medications available OTC that require prescriptions in the US. Antibiotics and common drugs are easily found. Pharmacists are helpful. Bring a list with generic names. Some medications may not be available — bring your supply. In tourist areas (Sharm el-Sheikh, Hurghada), pharmacies are well-stocked.
prescriptionRules: A prescription is required for prescription medications but enforcement varies. Antibiotics and many drugs available OTC. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's note in English.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are controlled substances. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. Declare at customs. A permit from the Egyptian Ministry of Health may be required.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Many codeine products are restricted. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotics (morphine, tramadol, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Strong narcotics require strict documentation and potentially a permit from Egyptian authorities.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names in English. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Check with the Egyptian consulate about import permits for controlled medications.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Required for visa on arrival / e-visa travelers. Strongly recommended for all travelers.
travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance is strongly recommended. Public hospitals are basic; private hospitals offer good care. Medical evacuation coverage is essential, especially for Red Sea diving injuries (which require treatment in a recompression chamber) and remote desert areas. Ensure coverage includes medical evacuation to Europe if needed.

recommended: Meningococcal meningitis (for travel during Hajj season)
Polio (ensure adult booster if traveling to certain areas)
vaccinations.notes: No required vaccinations for most travelers unless arriving from a yellow fever endemic country. COVID-19 requirements vary — check current entry requirements. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date. Consider hepatitis A and typhoid for all travelers.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink in Egypt. Use bottled or filtered water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice in drinks outside of hotels and reputable restaurants. Bottled water is very cheap and widely available. Waterborne diseases are a risk if you consume tap water.
foodSafetyTips: Be cautious with food from street vendors. In hotels, resorts, and reputable restaurants, food is generally safe. Avoid raw salads and uncooked foods outside of upscale establishments. Egyptian cuisine (koshari, grilled meats, falafel) from busy restaurants is generally safe. Avoid dairy products from informal sources. In Red Sea resorts, restaurants maintain good hygiene standards.
medicalTourismNote: Egypt is a niche medical tourism destination, primarily for cosmetic surgery and dental work. Costs are 50-70% lower than in the US and Europe. Cairo and Alexandria have JCI-accredited hospitals. Popular for hair transplants, cosmetic procedures, and fertility treatments.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Egypt. Emergency numbers (122/123/180), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, water safety, and travel insurance advice.

dentalCare.availability: Dental care is widely available and very affordable. Cairo and resort areas have modern dental clinics.
dentalCare.costRange: EGP 200-500 ($4-10) for consultation; EGP 500-2,000 ($10-40) for fillings; EGP 500-1,500 ($10-30) for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Egypt is an emerging dental tourism destination with prices 70-80% lower than Europe. Quality varies — stick to well-reviewed clinics in Cairo. Several JCI-accredited hospitals have dental departments.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Private hospital emergency departments handle dental emergencies. Many pharmacies can provide antibiotics and strong pain relief without prescription.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: Befrienders Worldwide: check befrienders.org for local contacts
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: English-speaking therapists available in Cairo through international clinics and private practices.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited but growing. Private practitioners in Cairo charge EGP 500-1,500 ($10-30) per session. Stigma around mental health remains strong.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Egypt's accessibility is limited. Modern hotels and international chains are accessible. Streets, temples, and pyramids have significant barriers for wheelchair users.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Private hospitals are generally accessible. Public hospitals have limited wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Cairo Metro has limited accessibility. Taxis are cheap but not wheelchair adapted. Uber is available in Cairo and offers the most flexible option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: The Pyramids and Valley of the Kings are extremely challenging for wheelchair users. Many tour operators offer adapted tours. Hotels in tourist areas often have accessible rooms. Hire a guide who can arrange assistance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Some indoor venues may request masks.
covidStatus.testing: Antigen and PCR tests available at pharmacies, clinics, and airports.
covidStatus.notes: Egypt removed all COVID entry restrictions. Heat-related illness and gastrointestinal issues are more common health concerns for tourists.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals may require upfront payment or a credit card deposit. Keep all receipts (iiSaalaat) and medical reports. International hospitals in Cairo can provide English documentation. For diving-related injuries at Red Sea resorts, contact your insurer immediately as recompression treatment is expensive.
